basic_identification.full_title: Specification for Copper Rods and Bars for General Engineering Purposes
basic_identification.sector_category: Metallurgical Engineering / Copper and Copper Alloys (approved by the Metallurgical Engineering Division Council and finalized by the Copper and Copper Alloys Sectional Committee of the Bureau of Indian Standards)

sectional_committee.name: Copper and Copper Alloys Sectional Committee

scope.summary: This standard specifies the requirements, dimensions, tolerances, chemical composition, mechanical properties, workmanship, finish, sampling, and testing of copper rods and bars intended for general and industrial engineering applications. It covers rods and bars in round, square, rectangular, and hexagonal shapes manufactured through extrusion, drawing, cold or hot rolling, forging, casting, or a combination of these.

certification_and_marking.certification_status: Strict Statutory Mandatory Certification. Under the 'Copper Products (Quality Control) Order' (QCO) issued by the Ministry of Commerce and Industry (DPIIT), Government of India, all copper rods and bars supplied for general engineering purposes must conform to IS 4171:1983 and carry the mandatory BIS Standard Mark (ISI Mark). Medium and large-scale enterprises had to comply by October 19, 2024, small enterprises by January 19, 2025, and micro enterprises by April 19, 2025. Manufacturing, importing, distributing, or stocking non-certified engineering copper rods in India is a punishable statutory offense under the Bureau of Indian Standards Act, 2016. Exemption is granted solely for export-oriented shipments. Precious metal hallmarking is completely inapplicable to industrial copper bars.

requirements.detail: Every commercial tag or label attached to bundles/coils of copper rods and bars, along with the accompanying test certificate, must bear the BIS Standard Mark (ISI Mark) along with the manufacturer's registered licence number (CM/L).

The standard covers rods and bars across four geometries: a) Round Bars/Rods; b) Square Rods/Bars; c) Rectangular Rods/Bars; d) Hexagonal Rods/Bars. Sizing bounds are as declared by the manufacturer for the scope of the licence.

The surface of the rods and bars must be clean, smooth, bright, and completely free from harmful defects such as severe scratches, cracks, inclusions, pitting, or oxidation scale. Non-coiled rods must be reasonably straight and free from twists.
To ensure dimensional accuracy for machining and assembly fits, the diameters or widths across flats must stay strictly within the tolerances defined in IS 2826.

When required by the purchaser to verify suitability for welding, brazing, or high-temperature processing under reducing atmospheres, specimens must undergo the Hydrogen Embrittlement test. Samples heated in a hydrogen atmosphere at 900°C must show zero microscopic or macroscopic surface cracking or blistering.
For factory audits, a sample size of 5 pieces of 5 cm length is required for chemical testing, and a 1-meter length of bar/rod is required for physical/mechanical tests.

The control unit (lot) comprises all copper bars/rods of the same size, shape, condition, and manufactured through the same manufacturing process from the same cast of raw material in a day. One random sample is tested from each heat/cast for chemical composition, and one sample per control unit for tensile properties.

plain_language_summary.summary: IS 4171 : 1983 is the mandatory national Indian Standard specification governing copper rods and bars (round, square, rectangular, and hexagonal) used across general and industrial engineering sectors—such as mechanical machinery, auto components, hardware fittings, and general manufacturing. Under India's statutory Copper Products Quality Control Order (QCO), all such copper rods and bars supplied or sold domestically must bear the BIS Standard Mark (ISI Mark) to ensure safety and quality. It regulates fabrication from Phosphorous Deoxidized non-arsenical Copper (minimum 99.90% purity) and specifies tempers in both the 'As manufactured' and 'Annealed' states. The standard enforces detailed mechanical and chemical requirements—including strict tolerances on cross-sectional dimensions (as per IS 2826), warpway/weftway breaking strength, minimum tensile strength (ranging between 130 to 270 MPa), 40% minimum elongation for annealed tempers, and an optional high-temperature hydrogen embrittlement test to verify structural jointing integrity.
